Liberation War Museum gets ICT verdicts' copies
2014-02-27T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/liberation-war-museum-gets-ict-verdicts-copies-13245

The two international crimes tribunals yesterday on their own initiative provided Liberation War Museum copies of the nine verdicts passed till date for preservation as historical documents. The copies were also provided to the tribunals' six judges and the Supreme Court library while the office of the tribunals' registrar kept one. The cases were over crimes against humanity and genocide committed during the 1971 Liberation War. “We also have plans to archive case proceedings,” the registrar, AKM Nasiruddin Mahmud, told The Daily Star during the handing over to the museum's Trustee Mofidul Haque at the former's office. Expressing gratitude, Mofidul said, “It is a priceless wealth for the nation.” Death penalty was handed down on Jamaat-e-Islami leaders Delawar Hossain Sayedee, Muhammad Kamaruzzaman and Ali Ahsan Mohammad Mojaheed, former Jamaat leader Abul Kalam Azad, Al-Badr leaders Chowdhury Mueen Uddin and Ashrafuzzaman Khan and BNP leader Salauddin Quader Chowdhury. A 90-year jail sentence was handed down on former Jamaat chief Ghulam Azam, former BNP minister Abdul Alim was jailed till death and Jamaat leader Abdul Quader Mollah sentenced to life term. The Supreme Court's Appellate Division, overruling the life term, sentenced Mollah to death. He was executed in December 2013. One of the tribunals' deputy registrars, Arunav Chakraborty, and another trustee of the museum, Akku Chowdhury, were present.
